lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

is_adopting.description: Whether the claimant is adopting the child.

child_has_moved_in.description: Whether the child being adopted has come to live with the claimant.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. 

To assess your eligibility, I need to ask you some questions. Let me start with the first one:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have one child I'm asking about. His name is Alex, and he's 11 years old. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I'm assessing eligibility for Alex, who is 11 years old.

Let me ask you the next question:

**Are you responsible for Alex? By this I mean, does Alex live with you, and do you look after him and pay for things like his food, clothes, and other needs?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, that's a bit complicated. Alex doesn't actually live with me yet - I'm in the process of adopting him and he hasn't come to live with me yet. But I am contributing towards his upkeep - I help with things like clothes and other expenses. I pay about £30 a week towards his needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for explaining that. Let me gather a bit more information about your situation.

**Where is Alex currently living while the adoption process is ongoing? Is he living with foster carers, in a care home, or with someone else?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's currently living with someone else - not in foster care or a care home. I'm going through the adoption process, but he just hasn't moved in with me yet.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. I need to understand a bit more about the adoption process and your current relationship with Alex.

**Has the adoption been legally finalized yet, or are you still waiting for the adoption order to be granted by the court?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm still waiting for the adoption order to be granted by the court. The legal process hasn't been finalized yet - that's why Alex hasn't come to live with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for that information. I need to read the official guidance to properly assess your situation. Let me check the eligibility rules.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for your patience. I've reviewed the official guidance. I need to ask one more important question:

**Does the person Alex is currently living with also claim or intend to claim Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, the person Alex is living with isn't claiming Child Benefit for him. Nobody else is claiming it.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Let me also ask:

**Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. I now have enough information to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me carefully consider your situation based on the official rules:

**Your situation:**
- Alex is 11 years old (under 16)
- You are in the process of adopting Alex, but the adoption order has not yet been granted by the court
- Alex does not currently live with you
- You contribute £30 per week towards Alex's upkeep (clothes and other expenses)
- Nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex
- You live in the UK

**Key rules from the guidance:**

According to the official guidance on adopting a child: "You can claim Child Benefit as soon as any child you're adopting comes to live with you - you do not have to wait until the adoption process is complete."

This clearly states that for adoption cases, you can claim Child Benefit when the child **comes to live with you**, not before.

The guidance on children living with someone else states you could continue to get payments if you contribute at least the same amount as Child Benefit. However, this applies to situations where you **previously** received Child Benefit and the child then goes to live with someone else.

In your case, Alex has not yet come to live with you, so you haven't reached the point where you can claim Child Benefit under the adoption rules, despite your financial contributions.

conversation.text:
Based on my assessment of your situation against the official Child Benefit rules, **you are currently not eligible** to claim Child Benefit for Alex.

Here's why:

The official guidance states that for adoption cases: *"You can claim Child Benefit as soon as any child you're adopting comes to live with you - you do not have to wait until the adoption process is complete."*

The key point is that Alex needs to **come to live with you** before you can claim Child Benefit. The good news is that you won't need to wait for the adoption order to be finalized by the court - you can claim as soon as Alex moves in with you.

Although you're contributing £30 per week towards Alex's upkeep, which is commendable, this doesn't qualify you for Child Benefit at this stage. The rules about making contributions apply to situations where someone was already receiving Child Benefit and then the child goes to live with someone else.

**What this means for you:** Once Alex comes to live with you as part of the adoption process, you'll be able to claim Child Benefit right away, even while waiting for the adoption to be legally finalized. At that point, you should make your claim promptly.
